title: Refuse an agent on the approve, reject and cancel routes in a dev run

A credentials run refuses an agent key (auth.rs:667-669). With an AI watch officer on the run, the dev path should refuse agents as the others do. Found while mapping for docs/design/watch-officer.md.

title: Menu drops the AI watch officer when switching scenarios
description: The main menu's AI choice defaults to None for each start (so the person's subscription is never used without choosing). Switching from a run started with AI=claude to another scenario from the menu starts it with no officer unless the person picks Claude again; on 2026-11-27 a wind-event run started that way with no officer and nothing triaged. Options: remember the last AI choice in the browser (localStorage), or carry the running run's choice into the next start, keeping None as the first-time default.

title: FLEETMESH_RATE speeds the conditions' clock but not the delivery runtime
description: scripts/scenario.sh and the Makefile describe FLEETMESH_RATE=5 as 'a faster scenario clock', but the bridge's delivery runtime (parcel releases, scripted events, GET /api/parcels elapsed_s; delivery_rt.rs elapsed()) runs on the engine clock in real seconds. Only tidewater's and the space segment's clock (FLEETMESH_AT + elapsed x rate, clock.rs) speed up. Seen live 2026-11-27: harbour-city at 5x reported 202 s elapsed after 200 s. Either drive the runtime from the scenario clock or say what the rate does. The menu no longer offers a rate (fleetmesh-x3k follow-up).

title: An agent can withdraw its own order after an operator approved it
description: AgentPort::withdraw allows Void from approved (intent.rs:781; engine.rs:4220-4241), so an agent can undo an operator's approval of its proposal unless it passes if_state. Replay does not check who voided (replay.rs 1892-1897). Decide whether an approved order is still the agent's to withdraw. Found while mapping for docs/design/watch-officer.md.

title: A flapping alert is routed to the watch officer again each time it returns
description: Live 2026-11-27 (harbour-city, quarter size, officer on Claude): DRONE 2's lost_link alert came and went four times in a few minutes, and each return was routed to the officer as a new triage item (the alert id is the same; triage keys a record by it while it lasts, and a cleared one leaves). The officer correlated them as one incident, but each cost a wake. Consider keeping a cleared alert's record for a short while so its return rejoins it, or folding a flapping condition (wake.py already marks condition.flapping) into one item. Not a safety issue: every item still reaches the person.
